finding.access-control.team-missing.step: Run the endpoint-level migration for this Route. It creates the team, and the blocker clears on the next analysis.
finding.access-control.team-missing.summ: Group {team} has no GitHub team yet, so its repository access cannot be applied.
finding.access-control.team-missing.titl: The group's team does not exist yet
finding.branch-rules.branching-model.ste: Review the branch naming conventions on the target. Branch rules were created only from the patterns the source enforces.
finding.branch-rules.branching-model.sum: The source defines branch prefixes or development and production branches. GitHub has no branching model, so these are not created.
finding.branch-rules.branching-model.tit: The source uses a branching model
finding.branch-rules.configure-status-ch: After CI has run on the target, open the branch protection rule for {pattern} and select the required status checks.
The branch rule for {pattern} requires passing builds. GitHub needs the exact names of the checks, which exist only after CI has run on the target.
finding.branch-rules.unknown-kind.step.1: Recreate the restriction by hand in GitHub if you still need it.
finding.branch-rules.unknown-kind.summar: These restriction kinds have no GitHub equivalent and were not translated: {kinds}.
finding.branch-rules.unknown-kind.title: Some branch restrictions are not migrated
finding.change-requests.open.step.1: Merge or decline each Change Request on the source, then re-run the analysis. The preflight checks again before every Run.
finding.change-requests.open.summary: {count} open Change Request(s) on the source must be merged or declined before the migration can run: {ids}.
finding.change-requests.open.title: Close open Change Requests on the source
Review the owner list and merge the Change Request.
The CODEOWNERS file is in a Change Request on branch {branch}. The owners are the default reviewers from the source.
finding.deploy-keys.key-in-use.step.1: Generate a separate key pair for this repository. The command writes a fixed file name in the current directory and asks for a passphrase:
finding.deploy-keys.key-in-use.step.2: Store the private key in your secret manager, add the public key as a read-only deploy key, then delete the local copy of the private key.
finding.deploy-keys.key-in-use.step.3: Or use a machine user with its own SSH key, and grant it access to the repository.
finding.deploy-keys.key-in-use.summary: GitHub rejected the deploy key {keyName} because another repository or a user key already uses it.
finding.deploy-keys.key-in-use.title: A deploy key is already in use
finding.extras.downloads-not-migrated.st: Upload any downloads you still need as release assets on the target.
finding.extras.downloads-not-migrated.su: The source repository has {count} download(s), which are not migrated.
Export the issues, or record them somewhere else, if you need them.
finding.extras.issues-not-migrated.summa: The source repository has {count} issue(s), which are not migrated.
finding.extras.issues-not-migrated.title: Issues are not migrated
finding.extras.wiki-not-migrated.step.1: Copy the wiki content by hand if you need it on the target.
finding.extras.wiki-not-migrated.summary: The source repository has wiki content, which is not migrated.
finding.extras.wiki-not-migrated.title: The wiki is not migrated
finding.git-refs.blob-large.step.1: Consider moving it to Git LFS before cutover.
finding.git-refs.blob-large.summary: {path} is {size}. It is migrated, but large files slow pushes and clones.
finding.git-refs.blob-large.title: A large file will be migrated
finding.git-refs.blob-too-large.step.1: List every file above the limit in the source history:
finding.git-refs.blob-too-large.step.2: Move the file to Git LFS, or remove it from the history, then re-run the analysis. The blocker clears when no reachable file is over the limit.
finding.git-refs.blob-too-large.summary: {path} is {size}, which is over the {limit} limit for the target. The Run stops before it writes anything to the target.
finding.git-refs.blob-too-large.title: A file is too large to migrate
finding.git-refs.empty-repository.step.1: Confirm that an empty target is what you want. No other action is needed.
finding.git-refs.empty-repository.summar: The source repository has no branches or tags. The Migration creates an empty target repository.
finding.git-refs.empty-repository.title: The source has no refs
finding.git-refs.hidden-refs-skipped.ste: Check whether any of them matter. Recreate the ones you need on the target by hand.
finding.git-refs.hidden-refs-skipped.sum: These refs are outside branches and tags, so they are not migrated: {refs}.
finding.members.approve-invitations.step: Review the invitation candidates and approve an invitation batch. Nobody is invited without an approved batch.
finding.members.approve-invitations.summ: {count} unmapped member(s) with a known email address can be invited to the GitHub organization.
Ask the invitees to accept their organization invitations.
finding.members.pending-acceptance.summa: {count} invitation(s) to the GitHub organization have not been accepted yet.
finding.members.pending-acceptance.title: Wait for organization invitations
Open the identity mappings for this Route and confirm or exclude each suggested or unmapped identity.
{count} workspace member(s) have a suggested or unmapped identity. They are not invited until each mapping is confirmed or excluded.
finding.naming.collision.step.1: Open the naming rules or the naming override of one of the two Migrations, and give it a different planned target name.
finding.naming.collision.step.2: Re-run the analysis. Both Migrations stay blocked until no two source repositories produce the same name.
finding.naming.collision.summary: Two source repositories on this Route would both be created as {repository}. The comparison ignores case.
finding.naming.collision.title: Two repositories map to the same target name
finding.naming.invalid.step.1: Open the naming rule or the naming override for this Migration, and choose a name that passes validation.
finding.naming.invalid.step.2: Re-run the analysis to confirm that the blocker has cleared.
finding.naming.invalid.summary: The planned target name {repository} fails naming validation, so this Migration cannot run.
finding.naming.invalid.title: The planned target name is not valid
finding.org-secrets.set-value.step.1: Set each organization secret with the GitHub CLI, and make it available to all repositories:
finding.org-secrets.set-value.summary: git-migrator does not set secret values. These organization secrets must be set by hand in {namespace}: {names}.
finding.org-secrets.set-value.title: Set organization secret values
finding.pipelines.complete-translation.s: Open the Change Request, resolve each TODO(git-migrator) comment, and merge it. The original file is kept at .github/git-migrator/bitbucket-pipelines.yml for reference.
Parts of the pipeline have no equivalent on GitHub: {unsupported}. Each one is marked with a TODO(git-migrator) comment in {workflowPath}.
finding.pipelines.disabled.step.1: Enable pipelines on the source if you want the workflow, then re-run the analysis.
finding.pipelines.disabled.summary: A pipeline file exists, but pipelines are disabled on the source, so no workflow was generated.
finding.pipelines.disabled.title: Pipelines are disabled on the source
Review the workflow, adjust it if needed, and merge the Change Request.
finding.pipelines.review-and-merge.summa: The generated workflow {workflowPath} is in a Change Request on branch {branch}, so the change goes through review.
finding.pipelines.review-and-merge.title: Review and merge the generated workflow
finding.repository-settings.org-forking-: In the organization's settings, allow forking of private repositories, then re-run the migration task.
If you do not need forks on the target, mark this task done. The repository is migrated with forking disabled.
The GitHub organization does not allow private forks, so the repository's fork setting cannot be applied.
Forking is disabled in the organization
finding.secrets.set-value.step.1: Set each repository secret with the GitHub CLI. The CLI reads the value from a prompt or stdin, so it never appears in your shell history:
finding.secrets.set-value.step.2: For environment secrets, name the environment as well:
finding.secrets.set-value.summary: git-migrator does not set secret values. These secrets must be set by hand in {scope} on {repository}: {names}.
finding.secrets.set-value.title: Set secret values
finding.target.exists-nonempty.step.1: Check whether {repository} is the repository you intended. If it is not, change this Migration's planned target name.
finding.target.exists-nonempty.step.2: If the existing repository is safe to replace, empty it on the target by hand, then re-run the analysis. Do not do this if anyone still uses it.
finding.target.exists-nonempty.summary: {repository} already exists on the target, has refs, and was not created by this Migration, so it will not be overwritten.
finding.target.exists-nonempty.title: The target repository already has content
Find the other Migration that claims {repository}, and decide which of the two should keep it.
Change the naming override or naming rule of one Migration so its planned target name differs, then re-run the analysis.
Or roll back the other Migration, or clear its target through its own controls, and then re-run the analysis.
The target repository {repository} is claimed by another Migration on this Route, or two Migrations on this Route claim it.
finding.teams.set-membership.step.1: On GitHub, add the organization members who belong to the team {team}. Only existing organization members can be added.
finding.teams.set-membership.summary: The members of group {team} could not be read on the source, so team membership is not copied.
finding.teams.set-membership.title: Set team membership by hand
finding.teams.slug-collision.step.1: Change the planned slug for one of the groups in the Route's group mappings, then re-run the analysis.
finding.teams.slug-collision.summary: The groups {groups} would all become the GitHub team {team}.
finding.teams.slug-collision.title: Two groups share a team slug
finding.variables.name-invalid.step.1: Rename the variables in the source pipeline settings so each name is unique, upper-case and does not start with GITHUB_. Then re-run the analysis.
finding.variables.name-invalid.summary: These names cannot be used on GitHub, because they are not upper-case identifiers, start with GITHUB_, or collide after conversion: {names}.
finding.variables.name-invalid.title: Variable names are not valid on GitHub
In the repository's webhook settings on GitHub, add a webhook with this payload URL:
Set the content type to application/json and select these events: {events}. Leave the secret empty until the secret step is done.
finding.webhooks.recreate-manually.summa: The webhook for {targetUrlDisplay} is not on this Route's allowlist, so it was not created automatically.
finding.webhooks.recreate-manually.title: Create the webhook on the target
finding.webhooks.set-secret.step.1: Generate a new secret outside git-migrator. Set it on the GitHub webhook and on the service that receives its deliveries.
finding.webhooks.set-secret.summary: The webhook for {targetUrlDisplay} had a secret that cannot be read. git-migrator never creates or shows webhook secrets, so the GitHub webhook is created inactive and without one.
finding.webhooks.set-secret.title: Set a webhook secret
shared.accept-lossy.step.1: Review the difference at {paths} and decide whether the GitHub result is acceptable.
shared.accept-lossy.step.2: To accept it for this Migration only, accept this task. To accept it for every repository on the Route, add `{policyKey}` to the Route's accepted lossy policies.
shared.accept-lossy.summary: {paths} cannot be translated exactly to GitHub (policy key `{policyKey}`). Until the difference is accepted, the Migration needs attention.
shared.accept-lossy.title: Accept a lossy translation
shared.pending-invitation.step.1: Ask {principal} to accept the GitHub organization invitation.
shared.pending-invitation.step.2: After the invitation is accepted, the next resync applies the grant.
shared.pending-invitation.summary: {principal} in {facet} has an invitation that has not been accepted yet. The grant or membership is applied after it is accepted.
shared.pending-invitation.title: Wait for an invitation to be accepted
shared.unmapped-principal.step.1: Open the identity mappings for this Route, then confirm the match for {principal} or exclude that identity.
shared.unmapped-principal.step.2: Re-run the analysis after the mapping is confirmed, so the grant or membership is included.
shared.unmapped-principal.summary: {principal} appears in {facet} but has no confirmed identity mapping, so it is left out of the target.
shared.unmapped-principal.title: Map a principal
verification.codeowners: Parity completes this task once the default branch contains the CODEOWNERS file.
verification.deploy-key: Parity completes this task once the target has a deploy key with the same public key.
verification.hook: Parity completes this task once the target has a webhook with the same URL and events.
verification.members: Parity completes this task once each invitee is an organization member.
verification.pipelines: Parity completes this task once the default branch contains the generated workflow.
verification.principals: Parity completes this task once the target has the grant or membership.
verification.secrets: Parity completes this task once every listed secret name exists on the target.
verification.status-checks: Parity completes this task once the branch rule lists the required status checks.
verification.team-membership: Parity completes this task once the team has the expected members.
verification.webhook-secret: Parity completes this task once the target webhook has a secret and is active.
